description: High-performance self-smoothing polyurethane cement mortar from 3 to 6 mm
whereToUse: Mapefloor CPU+/MF is mainly used to create smooth polyurethane-cement based systems
as base layer for rough multi-layer systems (Mapefloor System CPU+/DP) for industrial floors
Mapefloor CPU+/MF is typically used in the chemical and pharmaceutical, textile and tanning industries
canning in general, sugar refineries, dairies, wineries and beverage companies in general
production and storage areas of food companies in general
freezing rooms and wherever high mechanical and chemical spillages and contact to hot liquids resistances are requested.
notFor: Do not apply Mapefloor CPU+/MF on wet substrates or on concrete younger than 7 days.
Do not dilute Mapefloor CPU+/MF with solvents or water.
Do not apply Mapefloor CPU+/MF on dusty or crumbly substrates.
Do not apply Mapefloor CPU+/MF on substrates contaminated by oil, grease, or dirt in general.
Do not apply Mapefloor CPU+/MF on ceramic substrates or stone materials in general with no appropriate specific preparation of the laying surface.

standards.value: complies with the requirements according to EN 13813
coating (C), according to PI, MC, PR, RC, IR principles
complies with the principles defined in EN 1504-9
Resistant to fungi and bacteria, certified according to ISO 846.
Hygienic and sanitizable; certified according to ISO 4628-1 Riboflavin test for cleaning validation.
Complies with standards applied in the foodstuffs sector EN 1186, EN 13130 and prCEN/TS 14234
Complies with all Indoor Air Comfort Gold emission requirements for indoor flooring systems

packaging: Mapefloor CPU+ Component A: 2 kg pack Mapefloor CPU+ Component B: 2.16 kg pack Mapefloor CPU+/MF Component C: 20 kg bag Mapecolor CPU+: 0.23 kg pack. Warning: Product consists of two packs of component A plus two packs of component B plus one sack of component C and two packs of Mapecolor CPU+.
storage: 12 months in the original sealed packaging and kept in a dry and sheltered place at temperatures between +10°C and +30°C. Components A and B can be damaged by frost. Mapefloor CPU+/MF part C is sensitive to humidity.
notes: 1) This is the international sheet (edition code ends 'en (IT)', Mapei S.p.A. Milano, website mapei.com), not a UAE edition. 2) Consumption is given only at four fixed points (scratch coat 1 mm, and 3, 4 and 6 mm) and is NOT linear per mm: approx. 1.7 kg/m2 at 1 mm, but 5.5 / 7 / 10 kg/m2 at 3 / 4 / 6 mm. No figure is printed for 5 mm and no per-mm formula is printed. The printed mix density is 1700 kg/m3. 3) No total kit weight is printed. The kit is 2 packs A (2 kg each) + 2 packs B (2.16 kg each) + 1 bag C (20 kg) + 2 packs Mapecolor CPU+ (0.23 kg each); summing those printed sizes gives 28.78 kg, but that total is my arithmetic, not a printed figure. The mixing ratio row prints component A as 2x2.0 and packaging as '2 kg pack'. 4) Primer consumption is not given: the sheet requires a preliminary layer of Mapefloor CPU+/Primer (or Primer SN fully broadcast with Quartz 0.9 on fully cured dry substrates with humidity < 4% and no thermal shock) and refers to those products' own data sheets. 5) Temperature statements differ by context: the description says thermal shock resistance up to +80°C and operating temperatures from -20°C to +70°C depending on thickness; the characteristics list gives 3 mm: -10°C up to +60°C, 4 mm: -15°C up to +70°C, 6 mm: -25°C up to +80°C. 6) Slip resistance is printed as 'Class I (wet indoor surfaces)' and 'Class II (dry indoor surfaces)' with no further values. 7) The Shore D row is printed as 'Shore D hardness after 28 days (DIN 53505)' with the value 83 landing inside the label in the text extraction, so the label was trimmed before '(DIN'. 8) In standards, AR0.5 / C50 / F15 are the 'Typical values' column of the table headed 'Requirements according to EN 13813 for cement screeds' (abrasion resistance BCA, compressive strength, flexural strength) and BFL-s1 is the reaction to fire class; the sheet does not print a combined EN 13813 designation string. 9) Product must be coloured with Mapecolor CPU+ pigment (grey, beige, red, green, ochre, blue, orange); only whole packs may be mixed.
